- The first slogan tee appeared in the 1930s, emblazoned with the “Good Housekeeping” slogan on a simple cotton shirt.  
- In the 1970s, the rise of the counter‑culture and punk movements turned tees into canvases for political and social statements, with bands like the Ramones and punk clubs printing their own logos.  
- The 1980s saw the ascent of corporate marketing; companies began producing “slogan tees” (e.g., “Yeezy”, “Just Do It”) to promote brand identity and tap into youth fashion.  
- The 1990s and early 2000s introduced the “Humor & Meme” era, where internet‑fueled jokes and viral quotes were printed on tees, creating a new niche of comedic apparel.  
- Today, the trend merges personalization and sustainability—custom print shops and eco‑friendly fabrics allow consumers to design unique slogan tees that reflect personal values while reducing environmental impact.
